subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should OpenClaw expose a synchronous plugin-level config pre-apply veto for persisted config mutations, and what ordering, timeout, actor metadata, and fail-closed semantics should it require?
rationale: This would create a new plugin/API security boundary around persisted config writes, so code inspection can show the gap but cannot choose the permanent trust and failure semantics.

options.title: Design guarded config-write veto hook
options.body: Approve a narrow plugin API contract that runs after built-in validation/preflight and before persistence, with explicit reject payloads, actor metadata, timeouts, recursion rules, and tests across RPC and shared mutation helpers.

options.title: Rely on built-in validation only
options.body: Decline the hook for now and keep protection in schema validation, SecretRef preflight, baseHash, destructive-array guards, and the fixed agent config-write allowlist.

options.title: Fold into broader preflight framework
options.body: Defer this request into the broader plugin/startup preflight design so one framework owns config, boot, and plugin validation semantics.

recommendation.title: Design guarded config-write veto hook
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow plugin API contract that runs after built-in validation/preflight and before persistence, with explicit reject payloads, actor metadata, timeouts, recursion rules, and tests across RPC and shared mutation helpers.

likelyOwner.reason: They posted the visible keep-open review and framed this as config validation/mutation product follow-up.
